name: Coforge
summary: Coforge, known as NIIT Technologies until 2020, organises its work around industries such as banking and financial services, insurance and travel, and its interviews often touch on that domain focus. Candidates commonly report an online assessment for fresher drives, technical interviews on fundamentals and projects, and an HR round; experienced candidates usually describe technical rounds with the team and a manager discussion.
rounds: Campus drive, online application or referral
Online assessment for many fresher drives: aptitude, English and coding
Technical interview on fundamentals, SQL and your projects
For experienced roles: a second technical round or a manager discussion
looks_for: Interest in its main industries, such as banking, insurance and travel
Interest in emerging technology (its stated vision is 'Engage with the Emerging')
A clear explanation of your projects and your own part
Reliability and teamwork on client work

covers: Your degree or experience and the technologies you know best
One project with your part in it and a result
Why this role, in under two minutes

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new subject area quickly, such as finance or travel, to do a piece of work.
covers: Why you needed it and how little you knew at the start
How you learned: reading, asking an expert, working through examples
What you delivered and how the new knowledge showed in it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with someone whose working style was very different from yours.
covers: The difference, described fairly
How you adjusted and what you agreed together
What you achieved and what you learned from their style

questions.text: Tell me about a time you caught a mistake before it reached a user or client.
covers: What the mistake was and how you spotted it
What you did and who you told
What it would have cost, and the check you added afterwards

questions.text: What's the hardest feedback you've received, and what did you do with it?
covers: The feedback and why it was hard to hear
What you changed in practice
How you know it worked

questions.text: How would a flight booking system stop two people from booking the same seat?
covers: The risk: two requests read the seat as free at the same moment
Holding a seat for a short time, with a lock or a conditional update in the database
Releasing held seats if payment fails, and what the user sees

questions.text: For domain-facing roles: explain the main steps of an insurance claim, and where software helps most.
covers: The steps: report the claim, check the policy, assess, approve or reject, pay
Where software helps: online forms, document upload, rules checks, fraud flags
What a customer cares about: speed, clear updates, fairness

questions.text: Explain the difference between unit, integration and regression testing.
covers: Unit tests check one small piece in isolation
Integration tests check parts working together, such as code and a database
Regression tests check that old features still work after a change

questions.text: What is a stored procedure, and when would you use one instead of application code?
covers: Saved SQL logic that runs inside the database
Good for heavy data work close to the data, or shared rules
Downsides: harder to test, version and move between databases

questions.text: What does a message queue do, and why might a payments system use one?
covers: It lets one part of a system send work to another without waiting
Benefits: absorbing spikes, retrying failures, keeping parts independent
Care needed: processing each payment once, ordering and dead-letter handling

questions.text: For experienced candidates: tell me about an integration with an outside system that failed in production. How was it fixed?
covers: The integration and what failed
How the team found the cause: logs, the partner's side, data formats
The fix, and what was added afterwards, such as retries, alerts or contract tests
Something specific: one of its industries, a technology focus or recent news
How that fits your interests or skills
What you'd like to learn first

questions.text: Which of the industries Coforge works in interests you most, and why?
covers: One industry, such as banking, insurance or travel, and what draws you
Something you already know about how it works
A problem in that industry you'd like to help solve

questions.text: Do you have any questions for us?
covers: One or two thoughtful questions about the team, the client domain or the first project
Nothing already answered on the careers site
A brief thank-you

tips: Pick one of Coforge's main industries (banking, insurance or travel) and learn its basic terms and a typical customer journey.
Revise SQL and testing basics; they come up across development and support roles.
If you mention a technology, be ready to describe one thing you built or fixed with it.
Read a recent Coforge press release or case study so 'why Coforge' is specific.

sources.title: Who we are: Coforge's industries, vision and mission (coforge.com)

rounds: Manager or client interview (for many roles)
